g.text: Note single-part arrows vs. whole-organ brackets (#3 & #8).
Click Tiles in the Word Bank to Place
Click any rounded label button to snap it into its target slot.
Open study clues, verify all 10 placements, or reset the board.
1. Pollination: Pollen grains from the anther land on the sticky stigma.
2. Germination: A pollen tube grows down the style into the ovary.
3. Seed & Fruit: Sperm fertilize the ovule (becomes seed); ovary swells into fruit.

g.text: Botanical Hints for All 10 Flower Structures
Mnemonic: “Sticky Stigma stands with Style above the Ovary”
• Target #1 (Top Tip): The Stigma is the sticky landing pad at the very top of the central column where pollen grains adhere.
• Target #2 (Slender Neck): The Style is the central pillar-like tube through which pollen tubes grow downward.
• Target #3 (Whole Left Bracket): The Pistil (or carpel) is the complete female organ combining #1 + #2 + #4.
• Target #4 (Swollen Base): The Ovary is the rounded chamber at the base containing egg-bearing ovules.
Mnemonic: “Sta-MEN = Male organ; Filament = Fine thread stalk”
• Target #7 (Golden Sac at Tip): The Anther is the bilobed capsule at the top of each stamen that produces pollen.
• Target #8 (Whole Right Bracket): The Stamen is the complete male reproductive unit (#7 Anther + #9 Filament).
• Target #9 (Thread-like Stalk): The Filament is the slender stem that elevates the anther into the path of pollinators.
Sterile whorls that protect the bud and attract pollinators
• Target #5 (Outer Green Leaf): The Sepal forms the outer green calyx that encloses and protects the unopened flower bud.
• Target #6 (Showy Pink Blade): The Petal forms the colorful corolla that visually guides bees and birds to nectar.
• Target #10 (Swollen Stem Cup): The Receptacle is the thickened base of the stem where all floral organs attach.
Tip: You can click any Word Bank tile on the main screen to test your memory.

g.text: Sticky, papillate apex at the top of the pistil specialized for
capturing and hydrating compatible pollen grains.
Slender column connecting the stigma to the ovary; contains
nutrient-rich transmitting tissue that guides pollen tubes.
The entire central female reproductive organ composed of
the stigma (#1), style (#2), and ovary (#4) collectively.
Swollen basal chamber of the pistil enclosing one or more
ovules; matures into the fruit after fertilization.
Leaf-like green outer whorl that encases and shields the
delicate developing flower bud before it opens.
Brightly pigmented lobe of the corolla that advertises nectar
and guides insect and avian pollinators to the reproductive organs.
Terminal bilobed pollen sacs of the stamen where microspores
undergo meiosis and mature into male pollen grains.
The complete pollen-producing male reproductive organ of
a flower, consisting of an anther (#7) supported by a filament (#9).
Slender, flexible stalk that supplies water and nutrients to
the anther and positions it for effective pollen dispersal.
Thickened, cup-shaped apex of the pedicel (flower stem)
that anchors and supports all four floral whorls above it.
